text:
William Karlsson has been a Golden Knight since the expansion draft, won a Cup and a Lady Byng in the colors, and played only 14 games last season. This fall he's healthy, playing nearly 18 minutes a night, and stuck on six points through 21 games, with two in his last ten.

We'd be patient. He has three goals on 5.3 expected, and the bigger gap is around him: Vegas has scored 11 fewer goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice, one of the unluckiest marks in the league. His line takes 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five. That's not dominant, but it's not the line of a player who has fallen off a cliff.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, from his short 2025-26, had him getting to the home-plate area at the 87th percentile among forwards and catching his share of passes across the slot. Those are the looks that usually go in. The concern is age and role: at 33, behind Jack Eichel and a hot Tomas Hertl line, he needs the bounces to turn soon.
